headline: Highest risk is medium: OpenBBTerminal can ingest shared MCP/API content and Superset can consume it without verification, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and compliance exposure in default pairings.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/FastAPI surfaces and uses a "connect once, consume everywhere" pattern, so attacker-controlled content can reach its outputs. Superset exposes a Superset API and could ingest those outputs as trusted analytics input. No shared channel is explicitly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal output is copied into Superset dashboards or API inputs without sanitization, injection content can propagate.
IF a shared MCP or file bridge is configured between the agents, prompt content can cross from OpenBBTerminal to Superset.
mitigations: Disable any shared MCP bridge between the agents.
Require a manual review step before Superset ingests OpenBBTerminal output.
Strip instructions and markup from OpenBBTerminal outputs before transfer.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data and requests secrets; Superset has allowlisted egress and can transmit data outward. Even without a documented shared filesystem, any copied workspace or API handoff can leak sensitive financial data from A into B's outbound traffic.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal outputs financial or licensed data into a shared workspace, Superset can read and forward it.
IF Superset is configured to query external services with OpenBBTerminal-derived inputs, those inputs may leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not pass secrets or licensed data from OpenBBTerminal to Superset.
Restrict Superset egress to internal destinations only.
Redact sensitive fields before any handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention rules on inter-agent transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or use unrestricted network egress; Superset only shows allowlisted egress and no write or git capability. Overlapping mutable-resource writes are not documented, so direct capability conflict appears limited.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, file conflicts become possible.
IF Superset is extended with write or git automation, concurrent mutation risk increases.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only on shared resources.
Avoid granting shared write access to the same directory.
Run only one agent at a time for mutable tasks.
Use separate git branches if write access is added.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable store.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can produce financial analysis outputs, and Superset can render or act on API-fed data. If Superset treats OpenBBTerminal output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into dashboards and decisions. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Superset ingests OpenBBTerminal-generated figures without validation, incorrect values can propagate.
IF downstream users rely on Superset dashboards as ground truth, a mistaken upstream analysis can affect decisions.
mitigations: Add a validation step before Superset ingestion.
Label OpenBBTerminal outputs as unverified.
Cross-check key figures against source data.
Limit automated refreshes from OpenBBTerminal outputs.
requires-engineering: implement schema and range checks on imported metrics.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data and handles contact secrets, while Superset has no documented compliance controls or residency guarantees here. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch if regulated data is moved into Superset, though the profiles do not prove a specific residency violation.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is exported from OpenBBTerminal into Superset, retention and access controls must match.
IF Superset stores or logs those records differently, compliance obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Avoid moving regulated data into Superset.
Review retention settings before any import.
Mask contact secrets before transfer.
Document the data flow and lawful basis.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems.
